TWO authored fields have no unambiguous destination in the legacy CurtainWallData and the mirror says so in its own words: (a) `materialId` — 'a SINGLE generic id. The legacy model has THREE candidate slots — mullionMaterialId, glazingMaterialId and systemTypeId — with different meanings … so the id's intent is not recoverable here'; (b) `panels[]` — 'an authored per-panel override; the legacy model describes panels through gridSystem + CurtainPanelSyncHandler, which derives them from the grid rather than accepting a list'.
fidelity.⭐ THE HONESTY BAR, MET: The mirror does not merely comment. It emits TWO RUNTIME console.warn's naming the element id, the dropped field, the reason and the visible consequence — :147-155 'The wall is mirrored WITHOUT it — its 3-D material comes from the builder's defaults, not from this id.' and :156-164 'the wall is mirrored with its GRID only and those panel overrides are not reflected in 3-D.' It also SUPPRESSES the materialId warning when materialId is merely the handler's fold of systemTypeId (:142-147, §CW90-PLAN-TYPE-PARITY) — so the warning fires only on a real loss. THIS IS THE STANDARD floor.json's hardcoded '#D4C4A8' fails.
